newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria protests over U.S. statement on bombings.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria protests over U.S. statement on bombings.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Tuesday protested to the United States over a statement by Washington on impending bomb attacks at Nigerian airports, officials said.
They said Foreign Minister Tom Ikimi summoned U.S. ambassador Walter Carrington from his base in Lagos to the capital Abuja and lodged "a strong protest".
"The minister said the statement was insensitive," an official who attended the meeting said.
The state news agency reported that Ikimi told reporters details in the statement on the expected dates of the blasts suggested Washington possessed information which it should share with Nigeria.
"It is important for me to know so that we could take action," Ikimi said.

A public announcement by the U.S. State Department on December 17 said it had information that bomb attacks might take place at Nigerian airports this month but did not say where this came from. It urged American citizens in Nigeria to be cautious.
The following day more than a dozen Nigerian soldiers were wounded when a bomb ripped apart a bus filled with troops.
Nigeria's relations with the United States, the biggest buyer of its main export crude oil, have been sour since the army annulled a presidential poll in 1993 to restore civil rule.
The situation worsened last year when General Sani Abacha's government defied international opinion and executed nine minority rights activists for murder.
Ikimi said the U.S. statement had "created hysteria among the citizenry and discouraged our traditional friends who normally visit Nigeria to spend their holidays at this time".
He said Nigeria was not happy with U.S. reaction to bombings in Nigeria, saying it was not consistent with U.S. attitude to bombing incidents in Britain, Israel and Saudi Arabia.
